issues.legal_issue: An eviction proceeding based on an unauthorized assignment may continue against the assignee alone after the assigning tenant ceases to exist without a successor.
material_facts: A tenant assigned the whole premises to another person and put that person in possession without the landlords’ consent.
The landlords began eviction proceedings against both the tenant and the assignee.
While the proceedings were pending, the tenant company was dissolved and removed from the proceedings, leaving the assignee in occupation.
issues.conclusion: The eviction proceedings could continue against the assignee alone, and an order for possession could be made against the assignee.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 14(1), proviso (b), the clauses specify circumstances in which possession may be recovered; they do not restrict the persons against whom an order may be made to the assigning tenant. Sections 18 and 25 support the conclusion that persons other than the tenant may be affected by, or be parties to, possession proceedings. The purpose of the proviso is to enable recovery of possession in the specified circumstances, including where the tenant has ceased to exist without a successor.

predicates.unauthorized_assignment_eviction_proceed: A landlord brought an eviction proceeding on the ground that the tenant assigned or transferred possession without the landlord’s consent.
predicates.tenant_ceased_to_exist_without_successor: The tenant ceased to exist during the proceeding and no successor could be substituted for it.
predicates.assignee_remained_in_occupation: The person who received the assignment remained in occupation of the premises.

issues.definition: When a landlord brings an eviction proceeding over an unauthorized assignment, the tenant ceases to exist without a successor, and the assignee remains in occupation, a possession order may be made against the assignee alone.

issues.legal_issue: A lease clause that includes the tenant’s assignees within the meaning of “lessee” does not, by itself, establish the landlord’s written consent to an assignment.
material_facts: The lease stated that the expression “lessee” would include the lessee’s representatives and assigns.
The lease did not expressly grant a right to assign with the landlord’s consent.
The tenant assigned the lease to the assignee, and the landlords disputed having consented to that assignment.
issues.conclusion: The lease clause did not amount to the landlords’ written consent to the assignment.
issues.legal_principle: For section 14(1), proviso (b), consent in writing may be general or specific, but a clause merely extending the meaning of “lessee” to include assigns does not expressly or by necessary implication constitute consent to an assignment. Sarkar J. also relied on Regional Properties Ltd. v. Frankenschwerth for the view that the relevant consent is direct consent to a contemplated assignment.

predicates.unauthorized_assignment_eviction_proceed: A landlord brought an eviction proceeding on the ground that the tenant assigned or transferred possession without the landlord’s consent.
predicates.lease_clause_only_includes_assignees_in_: The lease provided that references to the lessee included the lessee’s assigns, without expressly authorizing or consenting to an assignment.

issues.definition: In an eviction proceeding over an unauthorized assignment, a lease clause that only includes assigns within the meaning of lessee does not establish written consent.

issues.legal_issue: A contention first raised in the Supreme Court may be declined when it was not raised in the courts below.
material_facts: The appellant argued that the proceeding was not maintainable because the lease term had not expired.
The contention had not been raised in the courts below.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to allow the appellant to raise the contention for the first time on appeal.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the procedural principle that it may decline to entertain a contention raised for the first time on appeal when that contention was not presented to the courts below.

predicates.appeal_proceeding: A party presented a contention to a higher court in an appeal.
predicates.contention_not_raised_in_lower_courts: The party had not presented that contention to the courts below.

issues.definition: In an appeal, when a party raises a contention that was not presented to the courts below, the court may decline to consider it.
